## RabbitMQ Source & File Inventory — Answer to Joanna's Question

*(Read-only audit. No implementation changed. No stress test or regression rerun — this used a single, direct invocation of the existing, unmodified `SpringBootProjectGenerator.generateWithAuthoredTwin` against the real RedCollar BPMNs, writing output to a scratch location outside the repo so every path below is concrete and inspectable.)*

### 1. MetaML Workbench generator source (where RabbitMQ code is *generated from*)

All in one file — but spread across **9 distinct methods**, not one:

**[SpringBootProjectGenerator.java](backend/workbench/src/main/java/com/metaml/workbench/generation/SpringBootProjectGenerator.java)**

| Method | Line | What it generates |
|---|---|---|
| `generateWithAuthoredTwin(...)` | 140 | Orchestrator — calls everything below, once per generated project |
| `mapSignalToGatedTwinTopic(BpmnModelInstance)` | 613 | Reads the Twin BPMN's catch-events/sequence-flows to determine which Twin activity each signal gates |
| `assignActivityQueueIdentities(String, List<String>)` | 656 | Computes the actual task/response queue names + routing keys, one pair per Twin activity |
| `writeRabbitMqMessaging(Path, String, String, List, Map)` | 693 | **Writes the 5 Java files** listed in §2 below |
| `writeSignalBroadcaster(Path, String, Set)` | 1073 | Writes `SignalBroadcaster.java` — the class that actually calls the publishers/listeners at runtime |
| `namespaceRootFor(String, String)` | 287 | Derives the queue-namespace root (`redcollar`, `automotive`, etc.) from the Manuf/Twin process keys |
| `dotPrefix(String)` | 268 | Helper for the above |
| `pascalCaseToKebabCase(String)` | 571 | Turns a BPMN topic name (`SamplingTwin`) into a queue-name slug (`sampling-twin`) |
| `sanitizeForKebabSegment(String)` | 584 | Sanitizes that slug to valid RabbitMQ identifier characters |

### 2. Actual generated RabbitMQ Java files

**Generated project root** (this run):
`C:\Users\Nirman\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Nirman-Desktop-ITP-a\081b1557-8ec0-43ab-8c0c-4fff42877505\scratchpad\rabbitmq-inventory-generated-project\fd97901d-e2b9-499f-84fc-2b712bf7f6c1`

**Source root:** `...\fd97901d-...\src\main\java\com\metaml\targetplatform\redcollarmanuf\`
**Messaging directory:** `...\redcollarmanuf\messaging\`

The 5 files you asked about — **actual class names match exactly what you expected:**

| File (exact path under `...\redcollarmanuf\messaging\`) | Package | Class | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RabbitMqConfig.java` | `com.metaml.targetplatform.redcollarmanuf.messaging` | `RabbitMqConfig` | Declares the exchange, and one queue+binding pair per Twin activity (20 queues for RedCollar), gated on `metaml.messaging.enabled` |
| `TaskQueuePublisher.java` | same | `TaskQueuePublisher` | Main→Twin: publishes a task message to an activity's task queue |
| `TaskQueueListener.java` | same | `TaskQueueListener` | Twin side: consumes a task message and performs the actual Camunda `signalEventReceived` releasing Twin's waiting execution |
| `ResponseQueuePublisher.java` | same | `ResponseQueuePublisher` | Twin→Main: publishes a completion message to an activity's response queue |
| `ResponseQueueListener.java` | same | `ResponseQueueListener` | Main side: consumes the response and releases Main's waiting execution |

**Plus the file that actually *drives* all of the above at runtime** (not one of your 5, but essential — without it nothing publishes anything):
`...\redcollarmanuf\signal\SignalBroadcaster.java` — package `com.metaml.targetplatform.redcollarmanuf.signal`, class `SignalBroadcaster`. Ticks every 1s, decides when a Main/Twin signal handoff is ready, and calls `TaskQueuePublisher`/`ResponseQueuePublisher`.

**Important — there is a second, separate RabbitMQ-backed system also present, which is NOT what answers "queue per activity":**
The template ships its own pre-existing, generic component-to-component messaging package (`MessagingConfig.java`, `MessagingTopology.java`, `HarnessMessagePublisher.java`, `HarnessMessage.java`, `ManufacturingMessageListener.java`, `TwinMessageListener.java`, `ExternalComponentStubListener.java`, plus `bridge/NotificationBridge.java`) — same package (`...redcollarmanuf.messaging`), also genuinely Spring-AMQP-backed (`RabbitTemplate`, `@RabbitListener`), also gated by the same `metaml.messaging.enabled` flag. But it uses **6 fixed, hardcoded queue names** (`machines.requests`, `twin.stage.updates`, `gateway.qc.requests`, etc. — see `MessagingTopology.java`), not one per BPMN activity, and fires only on manual REST `/complete` calls, not on signal barriers. **This is a different, older mechanism from before Joanna's per-activity requirement — the 5 files in the table above are the ones that satisfy it.**

### 3. The flow

```
MetaML Workbench generator
  SpringBootProjectGenerator.generateWithAuthoredTwin()
        ↓ (reads Twin BPMN's signals + external-task topics)
  mapSignalToGatedTwinTopic() + assignActivityQueueIdentities()
        ↓ (writes source files)
  writeRabbitMqMessaging() → RabbitMqConfig.java, TaskQueuePublisher.java,
                              TaskQueueListener.java, ResponseQueuePublisher.java,
                              ResponseQueueListener.java
  writeSignalBroadcaster() → SignalBroadcaster.java
        ↓ (at runtime, in the generated app)
  RabbitMqConfig declares exchange + N task/response queue pairs on the real broker
        ↓
  SignalBroadcaster sees Main waiting on a shared signal → TaskQueuePublisher publishes
  to that activity's TASK QUEUE
        ↓
  TaskQueueListener (Twin side) consumes it → releases Twin's waiting execution →
  Twin's external-task worker runs the activity
        ↓
  SignalBroadcaster (Twin side) sees completion → ResponseQueuePublisher publishes to
  that activity's RESPONSE QUEUE
        ↓
  ResponseQueueListener (Main side) consumes it → releases Main/Proxy's waiting
  execution → Main continues
```

### One property controls whether any of this is live
`metaml.messaging.enabled=false` by default in the generated project's `application.properties` (line 35) — set to `true` (with `spring.rabbitmq.host`/`port` reachable) to activate real broker traffic for both systems described above.
